quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
Blue with white lettering or symbols
White with black lettering or symbols
Red with white lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all controls before you ride.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard
Swerve back and forth across the surface
Ride on the shoulder instead of the grooves

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Swerving side to side is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you feel tired while riding
When you slow down where other drivers won't expect it
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your turn signals are broken

questions.correctAnswerText: When you slow down where other drivers won't expect it
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to wobble or shake?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Broken brakes
A balanced load
Strong wind

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers can see you as easily as they see larger vehicles
Other drivers cannot see you
You don't need to make yourself visible
You should ride aggressively

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers cannot see you
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than larger vehicles, so they are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume that other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up
Sit far back so your arms stay straight
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Drag your feet on the ground

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle rather than support your weight. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: Which statement about the front brake is correct?

options.text: Use it only in emergencies
Use it only on slippery roads
It is less effective than the rear brake
It is safe to use if you use it properly

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it properly
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe if used correctly.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, which brake should you use?

options.text: The brake on the tire that is not flat
The brake on the tire that is flat
Both brakes
Neither brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake on the tire that is not flat
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your legs can absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lift the front wheel.

questions.question: When should you leave more space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: A two-second distance is normally safe. Leave more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet sides makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.
Once in a while.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: How can you stop other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Give other drivers dirty looks.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves no large space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try sharing the lane with you.

questions.question: How much attention does a motorcycle need compared to a car?

options.text: Less attention than a car.
More attention than a car.
Checks should only be done by a mechanic.
Service should only be done at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more often than a car. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop in the shortest distance. Use firm pressure and do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping.
Only on slippery roads.
Only in emergencies.
Only in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Where is the horn button on a motorcycle?

options.text: By the left handgrip.
By the right handgrip.
By the left footrest.
By the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, stop in the shortest distance by using both brakes. Try not to lock either brake.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Use no lights.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Stay in the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright or reflective clothing and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding next to another motorcyclist?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if you need to avoid a hazard.
It makes it easier to talk to them.
It makes it easier for cars to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if you need to avoid a hazard.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcyclist. This limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT take to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use high beams when safe, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead—their lights help show the road and warn of bumps.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects your steering.
The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike and makes it hard to see your mirrors.
You cannot use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.
